output.reason: This lens compares NL-derived contract structure (containment, initial-entry, endpoint, guard-disjointness, termination, event-consumer-coverage) against the exact closed FCSTM/ModelIR topology. Key findings: the collision-avoidance scope (CollisionAvoidance/collision_avoidance_deactive/active) is completely disconnected from the reachable AutonomousMode hierarchy at the root - there is no root-level edge into CollisionAvoidance, so its owner-level initial entry, both endpoint transitions, and the event-consumer-coverage obligation are all structurally unreachable even though the local edges exist verbatim. Also HighwayMode<->UrbanMode dynamic-shift transitions (NL11) exist as guarded R45RouteToken transitions rather than direct event-triggered transitions but resolve to the correct endpoints, so they are satisfied endpoint-wise. The NL6/NL10 termination-to-FinishState obligations are satisfied via direct or macro-routed edges but FinishState itself, once reached, is a genuine dead end (no further route), consistent with termination semantics being satisfied - not flagged. The most significant structural defect is the disconnected CollisionAvoidance composite, which requires a derived reachability contract (since no NL segment states "CollisionAvoidance must be reachable" directly, but NL12 establishes it as required operating behavior of the system) in addition to the already-supplied initial_entry and event_consumer_coverage contracts NL12-INITENTRY-1 and NL12-DERIVED-784991484ade71bffc0f.

I therefore derive one composite-reachability contract for CollisionAvoidance and reuse the supplied NL12-DERIVED-784991484ade71bffc0f event_consumer_coverage contract for the activation event, plus add a parallel derived event-consumer-coverage contract for the deactivation event referenced in NL13. I also inspect the two termination contracts (NL6, NL10) for FinishState: FinishState is a leaf inside HighwayMode with only outgoing edges to [*] (route-token driven exits back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode/root), meaning it is a genuine terminal sink with no cycle back into itself, so termination is structurally stable for those two contracts and I omit them. I omit the endpoint-existence obligations that are already satisfied by exact matching transitions (verified against inspection-equivalent transitions), keeping only the behaviorally consequential gaps.

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, stable termination, and cross-wrapper reachability. The closed FCSTM shows CollisionAvoidance and its two substates are structurally declared but never reachable from the machine root (no edge from AutonomousMode/root into CollisionAvoidance exists in the transition inventory), so both collision-avoidance transitions (activation and deactivation) have zero reachable consumers despite being declared. This is a distinct root-reachability defect from the initial-entry defect (CollisionAvoidance does have its own local [*]->collision_avoidance_deactive edge, satisfying NL12-INITENTRY-1) and from the endpoint-existence facts (the activation/deactivation edges do exist, satisfying NL12-ENDPOINT-1 and NL13-ENDPOINT-1 as edges). I therefore derive one composite-reachability contract for CollisionAvoidance and reuse the supplied NL12-DERIVED-784991484ade71bffc0f event_consumer_coverage contract for the activation event, plus add a parallel derived event-consumer-coverage contract for the deactivation event referenced in NL13. I also inspect the two termination contracts (NL6, NL10) for FinishState: FinishState is a leaf inside HighwayMode with only outgoing edges to [*] (route-token driven exits back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode/root), meaning it is a genuine terminal sink with no cycle back into itself, so termination is structurally stable for those two contracts and I omit them. I omit the endpoint-existence obligations that are already satisfied by exact matching transitions (verified against inspection-equivalent transitions), keeping only the behaviorally consequential gaps.

issues.observed: The exact local initial edge CollisionAvoidance.[*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive exists (transition:line:86, tr_0026) targeting the correct state, but the entire owner CollisionAvoidance composite is unreachable from the model root (no edge from AutonomousMode/root ever enters CollisionAvoidance), so this initial-entry edge can never fire in any execution.
issues.reason: Per frontier discipline, owner default entry and root reachability are independent properties, but a present local edge whose owning composite is never entered cannot deliver the normative effective starting point NL12 requires ('the collision avoidance system is initially in...'); this is preserved as a predicate-null W1 candidate distinct from the reachability defect on CollisionAvoidance itself, since S2 cannot express the compounded semantics of local edge + unreachable owner.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The local owner-scoped edge itself is syntactically well-formed and targets the exact required state, so a strict reading of only the local owner/target relation is satisfied; the defect is arguably purely a root-reachability problem, not an initial-entry malformation.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance owner-local initial edge exists but is structurally unreachable from root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions row for transition:line:87 (source=collision_avoidance_deactive,target=collision_avoidance_active,reachable_from_initial=false); verify_facts.non_proved event-consumer check for transition:line:87 status=refuted.
issues.expected: collision_avoidance_deactive must transition to collision_avoidance_active under the stated composite guard, and this transition must be exercisable within the executing model.
issues.observed: The exact transition (transition:line:87) has resolved_source_ref=state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:84 and resolved_target_ref=state:collision_avoidance_active:line:85 with trigger matching the composite condition, but reachable_from_initial=false for both source and target; verify_facts explicitly refutes event-consumer reachability for this exact transition.
issues.reason: Although endpoint identity is exact, the frontier discipline requires that a present exact endpoint does not by itself discharge the contract when its scope is unreachable; because the deterministic event-consumer check explicitly refutes this transition's reachable consumption, the endpoint-level obligation cannot be certified satisfied and remains an open W1 candidate tied to the same locus.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition's own source/target endpoints are exactly correct per the source/model identity; the unreachability stems entirely from the enclosing CollisionAvoidance composite never being entered, which is a distinct upstream reachability defect and might be viewed as not a wrong_target/endpoint fault at all.
issues.title: collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active edge exists but is unreachable due to disconnected owner scope

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions row for transition:line:88; verify_facts.non_proved event-consumer check for transition:line:88 status=refuted.
issues.expected: collision_avoidance_active must transition back to collision_avoidance_deactive under the stated guard, exercisable within the executing model.
issues.observed: The exact transition (transition:line:88) resolves source=state:collision_avoidance_active:line:85 and target=state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:84 with the correct trigger, but both states have reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts explicitly refutes the event-consumer check for this transition.
issues.reason: Consistent with the deactivate->active pair, the endpoint cannot be certified operationally satisfied while its exact consumer reachability is refuted by deterministic facts, so it remains an open candidate tied to the same unreachable-scope root cause.
issues.requirement_quote: Once in the collision_avoidance_active state, the collision avoidance system returns to the collision_avoidance_deactive state when there is no active danger, as indicated by the conditions `front_inactive`, `rear_inactive`, and `pedestrian_inactive`.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Endpoint identity is exact per source/model comparison; the defect is caused entirely by the enclosing composite's disconnection from root, not by any local misrouting of this specific edge.
issues.title: collision_avoidance_active -> collision_avoidance_deactive edge exists but is unreachable due to disconnected owner scope

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for event=pedestrian_detected_dist_to_rear_5_vel_30_dist_to_front_15_in_HighwayMode_dist_to_front_10_in_UrbanMode showing reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE line null refs=[transition:line:87]; verify_facts.non_proved entry check_id=event-consumer:pedestrian_detected...status=refuted.
issues.expected: The collision avoidance activation event must be consumable/evaluated across the collision avoidance scope regardless of which driving mode (HighwayMode/UrbanMode) is active, per NL12's explicit cross-mode guard language (`in highway mode` / `in urban mode`).
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers lists declared_ref=event:pedestrian_detected...:line:14 with consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:87] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (empty); diagnostics report EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for this event; verify_facts explicitly refutes the event-consumer check.
issues.reason: This is the canonical declared-but-unreachable-consumer pattern the protocol calls out: a declared consumer with no consumer reachable in the contract's required operating scope violates the stronger reachable-consumer-coverage property even though the transition and guard are structurally exact.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The declared consumer transition exists exactly as authored with the exact composite guard; the absence of reachability is entirely attributable to the separate CollisionAvoidance-scope reachability defect rather than any narrowing or omission of the consumer transition itself.
issues.title: Collision avoidance activation event has declared consumers but zero reachable consumers across the whole model

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.states row CollisionAvoidance parent=null with no incoming transitions in exact_source_inventory.transitions; inspection_equivalent_facts.states state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.non_proved reachability:state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 status=refuted.
issues.expected: The CollisionAvoidance operating scope must be reachable from the model root so its described activation/deactivation behavior can ever execute alongside AutonomousMode.
issues.observed: exact_source_inventory contains no transition with target=CollisionAvoidance or any of its descendants from AutonomousMode, root, or any other state; inspection_equivalent_facts.states row for state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 has reachable_from_initial=false and outgoing_transition_refs=[]; verify_facts refutes reachability:state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 (and both its children).
issues.reason: NL12/NL13 together fully specify an operating system with an initial state and bidirectional transitions describing continuous safety-monitoring behavior that explicitly references both driving modes (HighwayMode/UrbanMode) contexts, implying it must operate concurrently with the AutonomousMode hierarchy; the closed model provides zero path from the reachable root/AutonomousMode graph into this composite, making all of its described behavior permanently dead, which is the narrowest exact structural gap consistent with cross-view frontier discipline for a required composite absent from root reachability.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met...
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL provides no explicit sentence demanding CollisionAvoidance be reachable from AutonomousMode/root; one could argue the two composites are intentionally described as separate top-level concurrent systems with only descriptive rather than structural obligations, so absence of a connecting edge might be a diagram-completeness gap rather than a violated requirement.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance composite is completely disconnected from the model root

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.states row source_id=CollisionAvoidance.collision_avoidance_deactive parent=CollisionAvoidance; inspection_equivalent_facts.states parent=CollisionAvoidance for collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.expected: collision_avoidance_deactive is contained within the collision avoidance scope.
issues.observed: collision_avoidance_deactive is declared as a direct child of CollisionAvoidance in both source inventory and closed FCSTM; containment itself is exact and satisfied.
issues.reason: Preserving the property distinction: containment is satisfied; the real behavioral defect is root reachability of the owning composite, captured separately.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Because containment is satisfied, this row is included only to make explicit that behavior_consequence attaches its actual defect (root reachability) to the new derived contract rather than reinterpreting this satisfied containment obligation as a violation.
issues.title: collision_avoidance_deactive containment is satisfied locally but its owner is unreachable

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states (CollisionAvoidance/collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active reachable_from_initial=false); diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL lines 83/84/85; verify_facts non_proved reachability checks for state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83, state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:84, state:collision_avoidance_active:line:85 all status=refuted; exact_source_inventory.transitions contains no edge into CollisionAvoidance.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidance (and its substates) must be reachable from the machine root so the collision-avoidance monitoring behavior can actually run concurrently with AutonomousMode driving.
issues.observed: No transition in the complete exact source inventory (29 rows) or the closed FCSTM inventory targets CollisionAvoidance/collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active from any other scope; inspection_equivalent_facts marks all three states reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts confirms reachability refuted for all three.
issues.reason: A finite G1 reachability check from root to CollisionAvoidance fails deterministically across the complete closed transition inventory; this is a genuine cross-wrapper reachability defect distinct from the already-satisfied local initial-entry edge.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: PlantUML places CollisionAvoidance as a sibling top-level state with its own local [*] edge, which could be read as an intentionally separate orthogonal region rather than a defect; however, no concurrent-region separator or cross-wrapper composition mechanism connects it to root, and the NL frames collision avoidance as operating alongside the driving modes, so isolation prevents the described behavior from ever executing.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance composite is structurally isolated and unreachable from the machine root

issues.reason: This is the operational (not merely declarative) failure of the exact event_consumer_coverage contract: the frozen registry cannot express reachable-consumer coverage as a single predicate, so this remains a precise predicate-null W1 candidate tied to the exact declared consumer and root-unreachability facts.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition exists and is syntactically declared with the exact guard disjunction quoted by NL12, so a reviewer could argue declaration alone demonstrates the requirement is modeled; however, declaration-only presence does not establish that the vehicle can ever actually be in collision_avoidance_deactive during a run, since the enclosing composite itself is unreachable from root.
issues.title: Collision avoidance activation trigger has a declared consumer but no reachable consumer from root

issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for event front_inactive_rear_inactive_pedestrian_inactive lists consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:88] but reachable_consumer_state_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE flags this event; verify_facts marks the corresponding check status=refuted.
issues.reason: Same root-unreachability-driven operational coverage failure as the activation event, tracked as its own atomic candidate per the distinct NL13 obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: Once in the collision_avoidance_active state, the collision avoidance system returns to the collision_avoidance_deactive state when there is no active danger, as indicated by the conditions `front_inactive`, `rear_inactive`, and `pedestrian_inactive`.
